title: Provider-neutral harness seam and the dsh adapter
summary: Adds a provider-neutral `harness` module — a `Harness` trait, a `CommandRunner` seam, plain-data result/capability types, and in-memory fakes — plus the first concrete adapter, `DshHarness`, which drives `dsh --profile headless --json -` through a runner, parses newline-delimited JSON events, and derives changed files from `git status --porcelain=v1 -z`. Nothing in the neutral module names a harness; the adapter is the only place `dsh` appears, and a test scans the folder to keep it that way.

lanes.label: Factory caller
lanes.subtitle: osf crate
lanes.summary: The code that will drive a harness: it holds a `Harness` and a `CommandRunner` and receives a `HarnessResult`.

lanes.label: Neutral harness seam
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/harness
lanes.summary: Provider-neutral traits and plain data: `Harness`, `CommandRunner`, `HarnessTask`, `HarnessResult`, `HarnessCapabilities`, `HarnessError`, and the prompt builder.

lanes.label: dsh adapter
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/dsh_harness.rs
lanes.summary: The first concrete `Harness`: builds the headless command, parses JSONL events, reads changed files from git status, and reports capabilities.

lanes.label: External processes
lanes.subtitle: dsh and git
lanes.summary: The `dsh` binary and `git`, both reached only through a `CommandRunner`; the adapter starts no process itself.

nodes.label: Factory caller
nodes.subtitle: holds &dyn Harness + &dyn CommandRunner
nodes.summary: Existing factory code that will invoke a harness. It sees only the neutral trait objects and the plain-data result, so adding `dsh` changes nothing here.

nodes.label: Harness trait
nodes.subtitle: run(&dyn CommandRunner, &HarnessTask)
nodes.summary: The seam between the factory and an external coding harness. `run` executes one task; `capabilities` probes what the harness can do. Object-safe, so callers hold `&dyn Harness`.

nodes.label: CommandRunner trait
nodes.subtitle: run(&CommandSpec) -> CommandOutput
nodes.summary: Runs exactly one command with its own env, workdir, stdin and timeout, killing the process tree at the limit. The only place a process is started; the adapter never spawns anything itself.

nodes.label: Result and capability types
nodes.subtitle: HarnessTask, HarnessResult, Capability
nodes.summary: Plain serializable data for the journal: the task, the actor, the outcome (finished or asked), changed files, summed usage, and the eight capability fields. `Capability` distinguishes Supported, Unsupported and Unknown so a probe that cannot run is never mistaken for a missing feature.

nodes.label: build_prompt
nodes.subtitle: task text + three rules
nodes.summary: Appends the three standing rules — edit only inside the repository, never commit or push, add no dependency — to the task text. The no-commit rule is what makes the git-status diff trustworthy.

nodes.label: FakeRunner
nodes.subtitle: replays scripted CommandOutput
nodes.summary: An in-memory `CommandRunner` that replays scripted answers in order and records every `CommandSpec` it was handed, so tests can assert exactly which commands ran.

nodes.label: FakeHarness
nodes.subtitle: replays scripted HarnessResult
nodes.summary: An in-memory `Harness` that replays scripted results and records every task, letting a caller be tested against two different harnesses through one function.

nodes.label: DshHarness
nodes.subtitle: impl Harness for dsh
nodes.summary: The concrete adapter. It rejects an empty task, an empty repository path, or a dirty tree before starting the agent; runs the headless command; parses the events; re-reads git status; and reports the outcome, usage and changed files.

nodes.label: Command builders
nodes.subtitle: build_command, status_command, probe_command
nodes.summary: Pure functions that turn a `DshConfig` into a `CommandSpec`: the headless agent command reading the prompt on stdin, the NUL-separated git status command, and the version/help probes.

nodes.label: parse_events
nodes.subtitle: JSONL -> session, final, usage
nodes.summary: Reads newline-delimited JSON events: keeps the session id, the last final message, and sums the per-step token usage. A non-empty line that is not a JSON object is an error naming the line number.

nodes.label: parse_changed_files
nodes.subtitle: porcelain -z -> sorted paths
nodes.summary: Turns `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` output into sorted, deduplicated repository-relative paths, including a rename's original path. Ignored files and commits the agent made are invisible here, which is why the prompt forbids commits.

nodes.label: Capability probes
nodes.subtitle: probe_version, probe_headless
nodes.summary: Runs `--version` and, only if that succeeded, the headless `--help`, checking that the help promises `--json` and stdin input. A probe that cannot run yields Unknown, never Unsupported.

nodes.label: dsh binary
nodes.subtitle: pinned 0.2.0-rc.2
nodes.summary: The external coding harness. It reports no model name and no cost figure, has no mid-run stop, and emits no question event — the adapter states each of these as an unsupported capability rather than assuming it.

nodes.label: git
nodes.subtitle: status --porcelain=v1 -z
nodes.summary: Used twice per run — once to refuse a dirty tree before the agent starts, once to collect the files the agent changed.

nodes.label: Neutrality scanner
nodes.subtitle: harness_neutral.rs
nodes.summary: Reads every file in the neutral harness folder and fails if any supported agent name, or a container word, appears as a whole word. A second test proves the scanner can fail by pointing it at the dsh adapter.

nodes.label: End-to-end fake run test
nodes.subtitle: harness_fake_run.rs
nodes.summary: Drives a full run and a capability report through the trait objects with the in-memory fakes, covering created-file, question, non-zero exit, timeout, dirty tree and every capability branch.

edges.label: &dyn Harness
edges.summary: The caller holds the trait object, not a concrete adapter.

edges.label: run(&dyn CommandRunner, task)
edges.summary: The change's central move: a harness never starts a process itself, it asks a runner to. That is what makes the adapter testable with no binary present.

edges.label: impl Harness
edges.summary: The first concrete implementation of the neutral trait.

edges.label: build_command / status_command
edges.summary: Every command the adapter runs is built by a pure function first.

edges.label: parse_events(stdout)
edges.summary: The agent's stdout is reduced to session id, final message and summed usage.

edges.label: parse_changed_files(stdout)
edges.summary: Both the pre-run and post-run status outputs go through the same parser.

edges.label: capabilities(runner)
edges.summary: Capabilities are probed, not hard-coded, so a missing or mismatched binary reads as Unknown or Unsupported.

edges.label: build_prompt(task.text)
edges.summary: The task text is wrapped with the three standing rules before it reaches stdin.

edges.label: HarnessResult
edges.summary: The adapter's output is plain serializable data, ready for the journal.

edges.label: dsh --profile headless --json -
edges.summary: The one place a process is started. The prompt arrives on stdin and JSONL events come back on stdout.

edges.label: git status --porcelain=v1 -z
edges.summary: Run before the agent to refuse a dirty tree, and after it to collect changed files.

edges.label: impl CommandRunner
edges.summary: The in-memory double that lets the whole adapter be tested without a binary.

edges.label: impl Harness
edges.summary: A second harness, so a caller can be shown to work against more than one.

edges.label: scans src/harness
edges.summary: The test reads the neutral folder and fails if any agent name appears in it, keeping the seam provider-neutral as adapters are added.

edges.label: full run + capabilities
edges.summary: The end-to-end test drives the adapter through the trait objects only.

flows.title: One dsh task, from prompt to HarnessResult
flows.summary: A single run: refuse a dirty tree, hand the prompt to dsh on stdin, read JSONL events back, then ask git what changed and assemble the plain-data result.

messages.label: git status --porcelain=v1 -z
messages.note: A non-empty result rejects the run before the agent starts, naming the dirty files.

response.shape: { outcome: CommandOutcome, stdout: String, stderr: String }

messages.label: dsh --profile headless --json -
messages.note: The prompt, task text plus the three rules, is the child's stdin; the timeout is the task's.

messages.label: parse_events(stdout)
messages.note: Keeps the session id and the last final message, and sums the per-step token usage. A non-JSON line fails the run with its line number.

messages.label: git status --porcelain=v1 -z
messages.note: The same command as before the run; its output is the changed-file list.

response.shape: { outcome: CommandOutcome, stdout: String, stderr: String }

messages.label: HarnessResult
messages.note: A final message ending in '?' with no changed file becomes Asked; anything else is Finished. Model and cost stay unset because dsh reports neither.
